key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on the connections of analogue neural networks makes them much better suited to smooth continuous-control and physical-regression tasks than standard weight-only physical networks.
engineering_relevance: This could enable ultra-low-power hardware controllers and solvers for embedded robotics and solar maximum-power-point tracking, with projected CMOS operation around 30 µW.
method: Use Kolmogorov-Arnold-inspired connections that learn nonlinear functions instead of scalar weights
Implement the trainable functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays
Validate transfer to physical hardware and compare against multilayer perceptrons and a memristive simulation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the approach outperforms on smooth, continuously valued targets with far fewer nodes and connections, but not on classification-like decision boundaries, and it transfers across about 35,000 connections with quantified fidelity.
watch_item: The gain is task-dependent, so the architecture may not provide a parameter-efficiency advantage for discontinuous or classification-style problems.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
